title: W1 fix ineffective: review-submit _focus_seconds is hardcoded "0" — reference_form.js never populates it, so focus_seconds_reported is still always 0 for real browsers (still present since r1)
evidence: form_pages.gleam:239-243: html.input([ attribute.type_("hidden"), attribute.name("_focus_seconds"), attribute.value("0"), attribute("data-focus-seconds", ""), ]) ... reference_form.js:78: page.querySelectorAll(".ref-question"), 152: var section = form.closest(".ref-question"); 153: if (!section) return; 202-204: questions.forEach(function (section) { var form = section.querySelector("form"); if (form) form.addEventListener("submit", onSubmit); });
detail: The review form renders value="0" and lives in .ref-card, not .ref-question, so the only JS that fills data-focus-seconds never runs on it. Real browsers still submit 0; the new flow test posts 240 directly (crafted), proving plumbing, not browser behavior.
recommended_fix: Bind focus capture to the review submit (listener on [data-testid=reference-review-form], like the .ref-question path) so honest browsers actually send focus seconds; server clamp stays N7-deferred.

title: B1 fix is safe today but build_entity_url validates nothing: raw origin_domain trust rests entirely on the write-time allow-list
evidence: email_client.gleam:895-902: let domain = case origin_domain { "" -> "righttenantry.ie" d -> d } "https://" <> domain <> path ... vacancy_handler.gleam:473: let origin_domain = domain_helpers.validate_origin_domain(req) ... domain_helpers.gleam:43-52: case bare_host { "righttenantry.ie" | "www.righttenantry.ie" -> "righttenantry.ie" "localhost" -> "localhost:4000" _ -> case string.ends_with(bare_host, "-755972035138.europe-west1.run.app") { True -> bare_host False -> "righttenantry.ie" } }
detail: No open-redirect/SSRF today: origin_domain's only writer is validate_origin_domain (allow-list), the path is fixed UUIDs, the URL is escape_html'd and never fetched server-side. But build_entity_url interpolates the raw string with zero checks — a future writer (backfill/admin/import) storing a crafted domain would silently ship phishing CTAs in landlord emails.
recommended_fix: Defense in depth: validate/reject non-allow-listed domains inside build_entity_url (or a shared allow-list helper) at interpolation time, so future origin_domain writers cannot poison email CTAs.
